notes: WHAT WAS ALREADY COMMITTED AND WHAT THIS PASS FOUND. Two of his three rulings arrived as a WIP commit: iso back in STYLES, and the hand-off hub priced on `central`. The dispatch asked for both layers of the frozen reference to be RE-VERIFIED in the file's own order, spot first and then every style row through styleFitRaw. THE ORDER CAUGHT A WRONG TABLE, which is the whole value of the rule.

LAYER ONE, SPOT_REF: all fourteen terms reproduce to the thousandth, worst drift 0.0005 (pinScore mu 27.213 / sd 21.742 to the decimal). Measured family-pooled over all 10,000 cards, because the roll and pop handlers share one ruler and so do the two screeners - his own catch of 2026-09-30. Nothing in these rulings touches a spot formula or an attribute bar, so this is the expected result and it is CHECKED rather than assumed.

LAYER TWO, STYLE_REF: measured WHEEL -> startingFive -> styleFitRaw, no opponent, all 1,255 fives. Exactly ONE style's formula moved, so exactly one row may move. Eleven rows reproduce origin/main's frozen values to within 0.03 (worst: postup mu 0.0110 / sd 0.0293, pickpop mu 0.0102, horns mu 0.0085) and are LEFT EXACTLY AS THEY WERE. The WIP had re-stamped all twelve with that drift, which is the float the block's own opening paragraph forbids - 'if it floated, a regeneration that lifted every shooter would lift the mean with them and cancel itself out, and the board could never move'.

AND THE WIP's dho ROW REPRODUCES NO FORM OF THE SHIPPED FORMULA. It read mu 70.877 / sd 10.400. Measured: `central` on the five's best playvol gives 63.231 / 15.332; on the REST's best playvol, identical; half-weighted, 74.813 / 9.813; at a 50-point guard window instead of DHO_GUARD 25, 68.897 / 14.440; with `central` off altogether, 86.386 / 6.389 - which is this table's own PREVIOUS frozen row to 0.008, i.e. the one variant that does reproduce is the one from before the ruling. Five candidates measured, none within 2 points of 70.877. The row is now the measurement: mu 63.231, sd 15.332.

THE COST OF THE WRONG ROW WAS NOT COSMETIC, and this is the reusable lesson. An `sd` 1.47x too narrow makes one point of hand-off fit worth 1.47x what it is worth. That is why TWO CLIFF-CONTINUITY CASES were red (styleFit moving 24.83 points on one attribute point against a 17-point law, and the pnr z moving 34.26 against 34) and why the deviation tax law's PLAYSTYLE row read blind -1.56 against its -1.50 floor. Correcting the table took the failing-test count from 25 to 16 WITHOUT A SINGLE RE-POINT: nine of the 25 were the bad table, not the ruling.

THE PLAYSTYLE ROW IS GREEN AND NOT ONE CONSTANT WAS TUNED TO MAKE IT SO. It reads blind -1.34 / oracle +3.69 PASS, inside [-1.50, -0.30], with STYLE_SLOPE at his "Revert to 0.20". HIS 0.143 WAS NOT NEEDED AND IS NOT USED: it was the honest number for a row that was red, the row was red because of a mis-transcribed reference, and paying it would have cost a third of every tactic's worth to the scoreboard (mean |stylePts| 2.64 at 0.20 against 1.92 at 0.143) for headroom the board does not need. He has ruled on that constant twice in one day and the second ruling was to leave it; it is left. If a later round does want the headroom, the number is 0.143 = 0.25 x 8.56/15 and the file carries the derivation.

THE ONE RED HARNESS ROW IS THE RECAL DESK'S AND IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED: `hunt` oracle +0.498 against the +0.50 floor, two thousandths, from their own hunt 3.68 -> 3.75 in pipeline 231. No constant in src/engine/tactics.ts that this round owns moves it, and re-pointing somebody else's law row would hide it. 8 of 9 rows PASS; tests/tactics.test.ts's deviation-tax case fails on that row and on nothing else, exactly as it does on main.

THE SUBJECT LANDS INSIDE HIS OWN LIST. The Thunder '25 read the hand-off hub at 81.99 on Hartenstein, a fine passing big who is 23 points of play volume behind Gilgeous-Alexander. With `central` the hub leg is a sliver and dho reads 51.23, TENTH of twelve; the winning read is HELIO at 77.72 - 'Can be pnr/helio/balanced/iso' - with pnr 67.91 and iso 69.16 both also in his list and both above the hand-off. ISO'S RETURN NEEDED NO MEASUREMENT AND WAS CHECKED ANYWAY: its stored STYLE_REF row reproduces to 48.792 / 12.397 against the frozen 48.790 / 12.396, drift 0.002, so recal_226 retired the style without disturbing its reference and the row is left frozen. THE HAND-OFF'S SHARE GOING UP IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE AND THE MECHANISM IS ARITHMETIC, NOT A BUG: `central` cuts the raw fit on the many fives whose hub is not their creator and leaves the few whose hub IS alone, so the raw distribution's mean falls 23 points and its spread more than doubles (p50 85.7 -> 56.3, p90 95.5 -> 89.5, the ceiling mass 51 -> 37 fives). Standardising a distribution with a long LOWER tail lifts its upper tail: a five at raw 100 read z 81.99 against the old narrow reference and reads 85.97 against the new wide one WITH ITS RAW UNCHANGED. The fives that rise are exactly the right ones - Jokic, Sabonis, LeBron, Magic, Scottie Barnes - but the share is 15.1% of the board where it was 7.6%, and that is reported, not tuned.

THE CAMPAIGN LADDER CANNOT REORDER AND THAT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT MEASURED-LUCKY: src/data/opponents.json carries no style or tactics field at all (round, team, ab, season, champion, record, positions, players), the order is a function of the team dials, and no python, no src/engine/offense.ts, no rating and no card attribute moved. 7 of the 24 readable opening fives change the CAPTION a player sees - Pacers '26 pickpop -> iso, Nets '26 horns -> dho, Blazers '26 fiveout -> dho, Hawks '26 triangle -> dho, Raptors '26 motion -> dho, Lakers '26 dho -> horns, Spurs '26 dho -> iso - and every one of the 30 keeps its round number, its five and both dials.

cost: HIS THIRD RULING IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THIS ROUND, DELIBERATELY, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS WHY A FORMULA FIX WOULD BE WRONG. "2020' clippers cant be pindown. They arent even a knockdown shooting team. They can do pnr (Lou will in Harrel out (a tactic/team fit can change the starting 5)), Balanced". Three findings, all re-measured on this tree, so the next round starts from the reading instead of re-deriving it.

(1) A SPACING DRAG ON THE PIN-DOWN WOULD PUNISH THE WRONG TEAMS. By the engine's own cornerFit the Clippers '20 floor is BETTER spaced than the Pacers '96 - worst 41 / mean 59 against worst 34 / mean 51 on the z, worst 27 / mean 55 against worst 16 / mean 42 on the raw - and the Pacers are Reggie Miller's team, the pin-down archetype, which reads 87.39. So 'they aren't a knockdown shooting team' is not something a shooting term can be made to say about this five without taking the read off the five the set is named for.

(2) HIS OWN LINEUP CHANGE DOES MOVE THEM, AND NOT TO THE PICK-AND-ROLL. Swapping Lou Williams '20 in for Montrezl Harrell '20, exactly as he describes, takes the pin-down 82.17 -> 73.13 and from 1st to 4th. But the five then reads MOTION 85.03, with fiveout 80.03 and pickpop 73.34 ahead of the pin-down too; pnr reaches only 67.60 and balanced is 50.00 by construction. So his intuition that the pin-down is wrong for them IS reproduced, and his intuition about the destination is not.

(3) THE REAL CONTENT OF THAT RULING IS ARCHITECTURAL, AND IT IS A RULING HE HAS NOT MADE. `startingFive` picks one five and `bestStyle` then grades the twelve tactics on it, so the engine can never see that a team is a pick-and-roll team WITH A DIFFERENT LINEUP - his own parenthesis, 'a tactic/team fit can change the starting 5'. Making the tactic and the five chosen JOINTLY is a change to src/engine/bestfive.ts, not to src/engine/tactics.ts, and it would move every team's five and therefore every dial and the whole campaign ladder. It needs his word before anybody writes it.

THE ROUND'S OWN CLEAREST COST, MEASURED AND LEFT FOR HIS RULING: recal_213's pinned sentence 'no guard becomes a hub' goes from 0 of the 96 fives that READ the hand-off to 17 of 189 (1.4% of the board, up from 0%). The NOMINATION is unchanged - 48 short hubs on the wheel, exactly as recal_226 left it, because `central` prices the hub and never chooses him - but a POINT-GUARD hub is by definition his own five's best creator, so he pays nothing where every big whose guard runs the offence pays, and the widened reference then lets him win a five. The seventeen: Michael Ray Richardson '80/'81/'82, Jason Kidd '96/'06/'07/'08, Mark Jackson '97/'02, Andre Miller '01, Jose Calderon '12, Jeff Teague '14 and five more. THE FIX IS A SECOND HALF OF THE SET HE HAS NOT RULED ON (a height or bigness floor on the PRICE as well as on the nomination), so it is recorded in tests/tactics.test.ts beside the pinned rule and left for him.

FOUR PINNED READS MOVE AND ALL FOUR ARE RE-POINTED WITH THE RULING NAMED, NOT WIDENED: the Spurs '16 dho 73.27 -> pindown 65.45 (the FIFTH round running that his 'Motion, or balanced' is contradicted - their motion 55.51 and their bench's 90.73 are both byte-identical and the DECLINE is unchanged); the Grizzlies '17 dho 78.42 -> triangle 68.30 at the number the row already asserted; the Lakers '26 dho 81.99 -> horns 79.48 in tests/court.test.ts, where the ruling under test is about the SPOT and not the shape; the Knicks '02 pindown 65.11 -> dho 65.72, which is the guard-hub cost above.
